key_insight: A systematic benchmark across three controlled visual worlds shows that object-centric representations can improve compositional generalization in some visual reasoning settings, but advantages are context-dependent rather than universal.
problem_solved: Determines whether and when object-centric (OC) scene representations actually help models generalize to novel combinations of familiar concepts in visually rich Visual Question Answering tasks.
method: Introduce a controlled VQA benchmark spanning three simulated visual worlds: CLEVRTex, Super-CLEVR, and MOVi-C.
Compare object-centric models against non-OC baselines on multiple compositional generalization splits and measure performance under varying scene complexity and supervision.
Analyze when OC representations help (e.g., occlusion, relational queries, object counts) and when they do not, identifying dataset and task factors that modulate benefits.
impact: Provides practical guidance for ML practitioners on when to invest in object-centric architectures for visual reasoning: use OC representations when tasks emphasize explicit object-level reasoning and structure, but expect mixed returns for other settings. Helps prioritize model design and dataset choices for compositional generalization research.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram of object-centric vs. distributed scene representations (objects as slots vs. monolithic feature map).
Bar chart comparing model accuracy across the three datasets and multiple compositional splits (showing where OC helps/doesn't).
Schematic examples from each visual world (CLEVRTex, Super-CLEVR, MOVi-C) illustrating the kinds of compositional queries used.
Decision matrix or heatmap indicating task/dataset conditions (e.g., occlusion, relational complexity, supervision) that correlate with OC benefits.
paper_title: Are Object-Centric Representations Better At Compositional Generalization?
paper_authors: Ferdinand Kapl, Amir Mohammad Karimi Mamaghan, Maximilian Seitzer, Karl Henrik Johansson, Carsten Marr
